request.question:
Which packages have the highest share of public symbols without a docstring? Consider packages with at least 20 public symbols outside the tests and give the top five.

Requested output columns: package (string), public_symbols (integer), undocumented (integer), pct_undocumented (number).
Return every requested field using exactly its specified column alias. Preserve complete case-sensitive repository-relative paths and symbol IDs; do not substitute display names. Include all requested counts and provenance fields. Explain the query result in ordinary prose; do not emit placeholder text. These questions concern a static map of open-source Python code. After executing SQL, describe the returned rows and query assumptions. Questions asking which files, modules or symbols mean distinct identities, not one repeated row per matching import or call occurrence; preserve occurrence counts only when requested. Caller/callee graph questions include methods as well as standalone functions unless a symbol kind is explicitly restricted. Use files.is_test for test-file classification; test_links describe associations, not the complete set of test files. Use DOUBLE or DECIMAL, rather than single-precision REAL, for percentage calculations.
Return total public symbols, the undocumented count, and the undocumented percentage rounded to one decimal place. Order by pct_undocumented descending, then package ascending.

gold_sql:
SELECT f.package,
       COUNT(*) AS public_symbols,
       SUM(CASE WHEN s.summary_source = 'none' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS undocumented,
       ROUND(100.0 * SUM(CASE WHEN s.summary_source = 'none' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) / COUNT(*), 1) AS pct_undocumented
FROM code.symbols s
JOIN code.files f ON f.file_id = s.file_id
WHERE s.is_public AND NOT f.is_test
GROUP BY f.package
HAVING COUNT(*) >= 20
ORDER BY pct_undocumented DESC, f.package
LIMIT 5;
